key_insight: The paper argues that AI safety needs new mathematics to make AI systems legible, steerable, and cooperative with humans, with different mathematical fields contributing to different safety challenges.
engineering_relevance: For AI engineers, the message is to map safety problems to the right math toolkit—logic and game theory for cooperation, probability for uncertainty and agency, algebra for learned representations, and analysis/geometry for training and generalization.
method: Organizes the safety agenda by mathematical field instead of by AI subsystem
Connects each field to a specific safety function or failure mode
Ends each section with an open problem aimed at mathematicians new to AI safety
evidence_signal: The abstract is a conceptual survey and invitation rather than an empirical study, so it provides no data or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: The framework is broad and aspirational, so practical impact will depend on translating these mathematical ideas into testable AI system designs and benchmarks.
paper_title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
